description: Reconstruction choices for trace.spjass.v1 (scripts/spjass-trace.py). Observations: shots/spjass/observations.json. Every value here is either read from the TikTok (cited frame) or an assumption that is named as such.

rest.note: W-C faces away from goal.E with the puck behind its heel. Heading from the frame-100 blade pose; slot position: mean of the blade poses 124-128 (207.1-207.9 mm; frame 100: 209.4 mm). The script backs the figure off along its slot until the resting puck just touches the heel (the read pose overlaps the model puck by about 2 mm).

turn.note: Counter-clockwise turn (seen from above). Frames 124-128: blade poses from the toe marks. 121-123 are blurred or the toe is out of reach of the slot solution: the onset and the two intermediate keyframes are assumed (fast start, as the motion blur of 123 shows).

spin.note: Clockwise spin of about 350 deg from the frame-128 pose to the frame-133 pose (unwrapped) while W-C slides about 25 mm up its slot. Frames 129-132 are motion-blurred: the direction (clockwise) is seen in the slow demonstration (frames 790-880) and in the follow-through (133-140). The heading follows a monotone cubic through the frame-128 pose, the touching pose at the strike (shot) and the frame-133 pose; the lunge timing (lunge_extra_keyframes) is ASSUMED: nearly complete at the strike, as the frame-133 arc requires.

limitations: Recorded on another STIGA table (Byggmax/gyproc artwork): positions assume the canonical Play Off 21 slot layout (camera fit RMS 4 px, leave-one-out 8 px, about 1.5-3 mm).
The spoken explanation in the TikTok was not transcribed (no speech recognition available); the move is read from the pictures only.
The spin (frames 129-132) is motion-blurred: its clockwise direction is observed (slow demonstration, follow-through), its timing profile is assumed.

Shot direction: the observed shot (blurred frames 132-133) crosses the goal line at y = 36 mm, which would overlap the +y post of the preview goal (mouth width is a preview value). The reconstructed forehand contact sends the puck between the observed goalie pose and the post; the difference to the observed line is reported in checks.observations_vs_trace_mm.
Ice friction is a constant deceleration fitted to the observed slide; it is a reconstruction rule, not a measured coefficient.
E-G stands at its observed blade pose (frame 100) moved onto its slot; the other figures not in the trace stand in the static assembly pose (they do not appear in take 1 near the puck).
Blade, skate and stick geometry are the AI-modelled mold at the assumed preview scale; puck thickness and goal size are preview values; fixture axis assumed on the slot centreline.

alignment.note: puck observations relative to the canonical slot layout; 0 = as calibrated

shot.note: Strike where the backward-extended observed shot line (blurred frames 132-133, 52.8 mm per frame) meets the observed slide; the puck leaves at the observed speed. Direction: ASSUMED - the centre of the window of straight paths that clear the observed goalie pose and both posts of the preview goal (the observed blurred line, -1.3 deg, would enter 7.7 mm from the +y post centre and overlap it). W-C's heading at the strike: the model blade's front face touches the puck.
